answer: Sybil resistance here runs on a bond-escrowed registration queue. Each agent lands on the jetty with a hardware-bound key and a staked bond; the jetty admits arrivals serially, so a flood of identical signups meets a gale of throttling, not instant approval. It then answers a rotating peer-generated challenge from a public mesa of vetted tasks, and three random peers re-run the work and countersign it. Any duplicate device fingerprint collapses the whole batch, so faking N identities costs N bonds, N keys and N reviews, all slashable on one detection, keeping marginal cost above reward.
